correctness.rationale: The exact polar is given by coordinate and edge absolute-value inequalities. Reflecting one bipartition produces Stanley’s order polytope, yielding 2^n L(T)/n!; Ohsugi–Tsuchiya’s forest h* identity yields 2^n M(T)/n!. Their normalized product is M(T)L(T)/n!. Exhaustive Prüfer enumeration of every labeled tree through n=7, independent exact subset DPs for matchings and extensions, and reconstructible canonical isomorphism grouping yield 11 n=7 types and the unique spider maximum. Four separately computed convex-hull examples corroborate the volume normalizations without being used as infinite proofs. The result makes no statement for n>=8.

value.rationale: The tight, first tree-only extremal crossover is directly motivated by established graph-polytope Mahler extremal questions. It exhibits a nontrivial tradeoff: the path has more matchings (21 versus 20), yet the subdivided claw has enough additional linear extensions (288 versus 272) to win by an exact 1/105. This provides an exhaustive finite cutoff rather than an arbitrary isolated computation, together with an exact graph-invariant factorization for every tree.
